claim: PoseTracker is a service developed by Movelytics SAS.
quote: Welcome to PoseTracker, a service developed by Movelytics SAS.

claim: PoseTracker runs MoveNet on the phone and returns reps, angles and a form score.
quote: PoseTracker runs MoveNet on the phone, so the app gets keypoints, then reps, angles and a form score.

claim: 17 COCO keypoints, on-device.
quote: COCO keypoints, on-device, no video upload

claim: Keypoints need no API key.
quote: Keypoints need no API key. Try the snippet or see pricing .

claim: Freemium is limited to 200 tracking calls a month.
quote: Up to 200 tracking API calls monthly (strict limit)

claim: Freemium shows a Powered by PoseTracker link.
quote: Limited pose estimation data. Includes a Powered by PoseTracker link.

claim: Developer plan includes 1,000 calls a month with no cut above it.
quote: 1000 tracking API calls included monthly — no service cut above it

claim: Business plan quotas per 12-month period.
quote: 100k , 500k or 1M tracking API calls per 12-month period — no monthly cap

claim: Extra calls on paid plans are invoiced at €0.01 or covered by a higher plan.
quote: On paid plans, tracking keeps working for your users above the included calls: extra calls are counted and, within 14 days, we agree together on a higher plan or invoice them at €0.01 excl. VAT per call.

claim: The developer SDK targets React Native (Expo Go) and the web.
quote: Native pose estimation SDK for React Native (Expo Go) and the web. Free on-device keypoints, optional API-key exercise engine.

claim: The classic integration embeds the camera in a WebView or iframe.
quote: The classic PoseTracker integration: embed the camera in an existing WebView or iframe with one line of code.

claim: PoseTracker says it is not a medical device.
quote: It is not a medical device and it does not replace a clinician.

claim: Offline React Native package bundles MoveNet.
quote: The offline React Native package bundles the MoveNet model on the device, so inference needs no network; the light package fetches the model at runtime.

claim: The web SDK runs MoveNet over TensorFlow.js.
quote: The PoseTracker web SDK runs MoveNet in the browser over TensorFlow.js, with free on-device keypoints, from a script tag, an ESM import or a React wrapper.

claim: Keypoints are free; apiToken only for the movement engine.
quote: No. Keypoints are free. Pass apiToken only for the movement engine.

claim: The RN packages run MoveNet inside react-native-webview.
quote: The RN packages run MoveNet inside react-native-webview ( WebViewPoseView ).

claim: One call equals one open session.
quote: One call = one open session, not one exercise.

claim: With a key, internet is required to authenticate and meter.
quote: With a key, internet is required to authenticate and meter ( POST /api/sdk/configure , POST /api/sdk/track camera_start ).

claim: The SDK accepts external frames.
quote: startExercise() again while processFrame keeps running

claim: BlazePose is selectable on light and web packages.
quote: Select BlazePose with options.model = 'blazepose' on light / web (not via features ).

claim: KinesteX names its standardized movement tests.
quote: Rehab and telerehabilitation teams use KinesteX to guide home exercise programs and to run standardized movement tests such as Timed Up and Go, gait speed, sit-to-stand, balance stands, functional reach and shoulder range of motion.

claim: Same MoveNet engine available as native npm packages.
quote: For years it shipped as a single WebView/iframe API; today the same MoveNet engine is also available as native npm packages, so you pick how you integrate instead of being forced into an embed.

claim: PoseTracker's comparison describes KinesteX-style as a hosted camera/content embed.
quote: Hosted camera / content embed

claim: PoseTracker suggests a hosted WebView (KinesteX-style) if you want their workout UI.
quote: A hosted WebView (KinesteX-style) if you want their workout UI more than you want to own the camera.

claim: PoseTracker says KinesteX and Sency are often sales-led.
quote: KinesteX / Sency often sales-led. Treat quotes as current only from the vendor.

claim: PoseTracker has no first-party Flutter SDK.
quote: Flutter-only (no first-party Flutter SDK).

claim: No independent lab ranks these SDKs.
quote: No independent lab ranks these SDKs on a shared accuracy set. Compare architecture and constraints, then test your movements.

claim: Paid plans are not cut at the included calls.
quote: On paid plans with an included number of tracking API calls (Developer, Business 100k, 500k and 1M), PoseTracker does not cut the service when the included calls are reached: tracking keeps working for your end users and no error is returned to them.

claim: Managed plans are concluded outside the self-serve Developer checkout.
quote: Some Business plans are concluded directly with Movelytics SAS (a “managed plan”) rather than through the self-serve Developer checkout.

claim: KinesteX is a white-label SDK inside your app.
quote: A white-label SDK that coaches every rep through your users' own camera, inside your app.

claim: KinesteX's SDK list per its docs.
quote: Our white-label solution supports any camera-enabled device across Android, iOS, and web, with SDKs for Swift, Kotlin, Flutter, React Native and React (TypeScript), plus a plain HTML/JavaScript iframe integration for any web page or PWA.

claim: AI Trainer Chat is KinesteX's recommended starting point.
quote: Conversational AI personal trainer with in-app fitness assessment, personalized workout generation, post-workout check-ins, and next-session scheduling. The recommended starting point for new integrations.

claim: Camera Component streams motion events and pose landmarks on request.
quote: Build your own workout UI on top of our motion tracking. The camera component streams real-time motion events (reps, holds, form feedback, presence, activity, plus opt-in form state and framing hints) and, on request, pose landmarks. See real-time motion events .

claim: Requirements: iOS 14.0+ and Xcode 16.3+.
quote: iOS 14.0+ (Swift KinesteXAIKit , Xcode 16.3+)

claim: Requirements: Android 9+ (API 28).
quote: Android 9+ (API 28, Kotlin KinesteX-SDK-Kotlin )

claim: KinesteX's SwiftUI kit embeds the experience as a WebView.
quote: A SwiftUI package that embeds KinesteX’s AI-powered camera workout experience as a WebView.

claim: KinesteX's site counts 500+ exercises.
quote: 500+ exercises spanning cardio, strength, core, flexibility and mobility, so users have what they need to get fitter and move better.

claim: KinesteX supports 19 languages with right-to-left support.
quote: Yes. The SDK's guided workout experience supports 19 languages (English, Spanish, French, German, Dutch, Italian, Portuguese, Russian, Arabic, Hebrew, Hindi, Bengali, Indonesian, Danish, Greek, Chinese, Uzbek, Urdu, and Kazakh), with right-to-left support for Arabic, Hebrew, and Urdu.

claim: KinesteX's white-label solution carries no KinesteX logos.
quote: Yes, we offer a fully white-labeled solution, enabling seamless branding integration without any KinesteX logos or marks.

claim: KinesteX's pricing is per active user per month.
quote: The pricing per-active-user-per-month will smoothly go down as you scale and reach new tiers.

claim: KinesteX claims 97.2% accuracy.
quote: Our AI-powered motion tracking achieves 97.2% accuracy, offering feedback similar to a personal trainer.

claim: Ready-made Experiences take a week or less with one developer.
quote: Live in a week or less with one developer. We handle maintenance.

claim: KinesteX security page: camera and vision processing stays on-device.
quote: All camera and vision processing stays on-device; only pseudonymized movement data, session metrics, and an opaque partner-supplied user identifier ever reach KinesteX.

claim: KinesteX READMEs say optional edge processing.
quote: Ensures data security with optional edge processing (no cloud transmission).
